title: The Chinese writing system
summary: China's written history begins around 1200 BCE with inscriptions on tortoise shells and cattle bones used for divination in the Shang dynasty. These oracle bones hold the earliest evidence of full sentences in Chinese. The script evolved into the standard Chinese logographic writing system still in use today. UNESCO calls the inscriptions at Yin Xu testimony to one of the world's oldest writing systems.

uncertainty.note: Attested written history begins with oracle bone inscriptions from the reign of Wu Ding around 1200 BCE, continuing through the end of the Shang capital at Yinxu in 1046 BCE.

as_recorded.value: China’s written history begins with these inscriptions around 1200 BCE
Ancient Chinese writing evolved from the practice of divination during the Shang Dynasty (1600-1046 BCE)

where.historical_name: Yin (Yinxu), capital of the late Shang dynasty

importance.justification: A writing system in continuous use for over 3,000 years.

reviewer_note: Earlier marks on pottery may be early forms of Chinese graphs, so the start date is for full writing. The record covers its origin, not its later spread. The pin marks Yin Xu, near Anyang.
